resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §45 line 98: scope: The judge's facts are right. The finding still fails as a BLOCKING defect, on harm and on precedent.

What I verified:
- `grep -n -i leap curriculum/exercises/apt101-take-it-to-the-team.md` returns 0 hits.
- The maintainer block runs L93-120, and L98 is quoted exactly.
- `apt101-send-it-off.md` L124 does carry a **Leap test:** line.
- `rule.js pedagogy 45` gives the current wording: "Every exercise maintainer block: 3 observable outcomes … Story judge blocks ship on missing/unfalsifiable leap tests." The rule also carries an artefact carve-out: "leap test names ARTIFACT student now has + uses".
- §45 is not on the `check_workshop.md` N/A list, so scope lenses (b) and (e) do not exempt this file.
- No dated accept-note exists, so lens (c) does not help either.
- On the letter, the rule is breached.

Why it is not blocking:

(1) The harm claim restates the rule and is partly false. The judge says "nothing falsifiable says what the trio does by Monday beyond the artefact list." But the block already names a Monday-checkable outcome in the shape the carve-out asks for:
- L98: "a named first move per role in `team/monday.md`"
- L120: "The artefact is `team/monday.md`: a proposal the team decides, with each role's first move."
"Does `team/monday.md` name a first move for each role?" is a yes/no check on Monday. The proposed fix's first item repeats this word for word, so it relabels existing content. The other two items are already carried elsewhere:
- "Which assumption would sink it" → `assumptions.md` and `failure-stories.md` in Artefacts.
- "Which file they sent and what stayed behind" → the L100 phase-2 design.
The fix adds a label, not information.

(2) Nobody in the room is worse off. This is maintainer-only apparatus. The file already passed behavior @3d7fd713.

(3) Precedent in this same sweep. The identical finding (§45, no leap test, filed as blocking) on `apt101-build-your-product-memory.pedagogy.json` was refuted by both refuters on 2026-10-07. Its resolution note gives the same reasons: "The harm is the rule restated" and "other lines already carry the meaning". That file then got its leap test as a non-blocking finding (commit 761a20a3, now L118). Among the other APT101 pedagogy instances I checked, the same missing-leap-test REVISE was filed `blocking:false`. That covers send-it-off, map-the-story, keep-and-run-tonight, pick-the-outcome, write-what-good-means, make-your-piece and others. Blocking here alone is inconsistent grading.

(4) The rule names the story judge as the one that "blocks ship". A pedagogy judge escalating it to BLOCK goes past the rule's own stated enforcement point.

Correct disposition: downgrade to non-blocking and apply the leap-test line as a maintainer-block edit (no card needed). Do not hold ship on it. / harm: The judge has the facts right but the block is wrong. I ran `grep -n -i leap` on curriculum/exercises/apt101-take-it-to-the-team.md and got 0 hits. The maintainer block runs from `<!-- maintainer -->` to the View summary, about L93-120. apt101-send-it-off.md does carry "**Leap test:**" at L124, and check_pedagogy.md §45 (L115) does ask every exercise maintainer block for one. The finding still fails the harm lens.

(b) The harm is the rule restated, not a consequence. "Nothing falsifiable says what the trio does by Monday" only says the label is missing. Also, §45's blocking sentence is "Story judge blocks ship". It gives the story judge that power, not a pedagogy judge, so "§45 says missing leap tests block ship" overreads the rule for this class.

(d) Other lines already carry the meaning, so the fix only relabels them. The carve-out for artefact-led beats asks for the artefact the student now owns and uses. The block already names it twice:
- Role in Day 3 (L98, the line the judge quotes): "a named first move per role in `team/monday.md`".
- View summary: "The artefact is `team/monday.md`: a proposal the team decides, with each role's first move."
The judge's first proposed outcome is the same sentence again. The third (which file was sent, what stayed behind) is already the designed close of phase 2 in the Reuse line: "one thing that stayed on the sender's laptop".

(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. This is trainer-only apparatus, and the file passed behavior at 3d7fd713.

Precedent from this batch's sibling run, commit 761a20a3: the same §45 finding was filed as blocking on apt101-build-your-product-memory. Both refuters killed it on these same (b)/(d)/(a) grounds, and it is recorded under resolution.settled=refuted. On what-goes-in, write-the-bet and send-it-off the same gap was filed REVISE with blocking:false, and the leap tests were then added as non-blocking work. Of the 18 APT101 exercises, 10 have no leap test, so its absence here is not a lapse that marks this one file. Blocking it here would break that consistency.

Verdict: not a blocking defect. At most a non-blocking maintainer-block addition, which the orchestrator can apply the way Day 1 did.; pedagogy §47 line 113: harm: The judge's facts are right, but the harm doesn't hold up, so this is not BLOCKING.

The facts I checked: `grep -ci 'failure mode'` on curriculum/exercises/apt101-take-it-to-the-team.md returns 0. The maintainer block (L93-120) has no Failure modes line. apt101-send-it-off.md L122 does have one. The quote at L113 is exact.

Why the harm fails:

(d) The body already gives a recovery for each of the three failures the judge calls "unanswered":
- L67 handles the polished technical plan beside an empty people plan. It names that as "a finding" and gives the move: "Leave the gaps visible. They are Monday's questions."
- L79 handles the failure story that blames the team. It is the escape hatch, word for word: "Push back on the failure story if it blames the team for being slow. The old way stayed because it did the job well enough."
- L27 handles the post-it written after the run. It says to write it "Before running it", and adds "The run never sees the post-it."

Other recoveries are also in the body. For phase 2, L33 has the designer point at the line that went generic. For phase 3, L52: "point at the generic line and ask Claude to try that part again". For phase 6, L91: "A part with no name gets one now, or stays visibly empty". The Room line (L115) covers the trio pairing, how the file reaches the other trio, and the no-Miro-connector fallback. A trainer reading this page has a recovery move for every phase the judge names. The only gap is that the moves are not also collected into one line in the maintainer block.

(b) The harm sentence "The newest phases therefore have no trainer lookup" is §47's own wording (rule L119: "newest phase has no trainer lookup"). It restates the rule; it does not show anyone in the room being worse off.

(a) and precedent: this same §47 shape was filed against Day 1 siblings (write-the-bet, send-it-off, build-your-product-memory). Both lenses refuted it as blocking, recorded as `resolution.settled: refuted` in those instance JSONs.
